sources.entry: Obsidian - A second brain, for you, forever.

summary.name: Obsidian
summary.one_liner: Obsidian is a free, flexible note-taking app that stores your notes privately on your device, with linking, a graph view, and optional publishing of notes as websites.
use_cases: Linking ideas, people, places and books in personal notes
Building an online wiki or documentation site
Creating a digital garden of published notes
Keeping private notes offline on your device
summary.what_it_does: Obsidian is a notes app that stores notes privately on the user's device, so they are accessible offline. Notes can be linked to each other, and a interactive graph view shows relationships between notes. Users can extend it with community plugins and themes, and it uses open file formats. Obsidian Publish lets users publish notes as fast, mobile-friendly websites with themes, custom domains and password protection. The page also links to a Discord community, a discussion forum, and developer docs for building plugins and themes.
notable: Notes stored locally on device in open file formats
Bidirectional note links with interactive graph view
Thousands of community plugins and themes
Obsidian Publish turns notes into websites
caveats: Publishing via Obsidian Publish is a separate feature; its pricing is not stated on this page
Platform list is inferred from the listings (macOS) and the download prompt; the page does not enumerate platforms explicitly
